q: Consider the graph consisting of one central vertex joined to three outer vertices. In how many ways can its vertices be coloured using two colours so that no two adjacent vertices have the same colour? What happens with three colours? With $n$ colours? Find an expression $f(n)$ for the number of valid colourings. Now consider a different graph obtained by adding another vertex and edge. How does the number of valid colourings change? Does your expression $f(n)$ work for all graphs? More generally, if a new vertex is added and joined to every existing vertex, how does this affect the number of colourings?
